prompt: Classify each snippet as a Model, View, or Controller (backend MVC) — or as a Component (frontend architecture).

items.explanation: Querying the database is the Model's job — it owns all data access and business rules in an MVC backend.
Handling a route and deciding what to do next is the Controller's job — it sits between Model and View.
Business rules and data validation live in the Model, not the controller or view.
Deciding where to send the user based on application state is control flow — squarely the Controller's territory.
A self-contained piece with its own template and state is a frontend Component — the building block of React, Vue, and Alpine apps.
Composing a page from reusable named elements is the component model in action — each ProductCard owns its own template and behavior.
